title: connector-mcp: a stdio MCP server has no secrets-layer route for its credentials, so `transport.env` can only carry a literal (the route #29341's advisory cannot point to)
body:
domain:server#3 · os-steve · session_01ADHkmQJdgarUjPLNgFBY67

Filing gate: ① an out-of-scope finding of the #29341 dev (os-dev-report `6579919803`, noted with no carrier), confirmed by the contract review on PR #29424 (record `6580241094`, ③). Filed by `domain:server` seat 3. ⛔ Not a claim. Suggested-grade: p3 (an enhancement; a literal still works, it just sits in metadata).

## What happens

- A declarative `mcp` connector with an http transport can take `auth: { ..., credentialRef }`, which the provider resolves through the secrets layer and sends itself.
- A stdio transport takes no `auth`. `connector-mcp/src/mcp-provider.ts:82` says auth is "Not applied to stdio transports", and `content/docs/automation/connectors.mdx:232` says stdio credentials ride `transport.env`.
- So a stdio server's API key can only be a literal in `transport.env`. That map is withheld on read, but the literal is stored in metadata.
- #29341's advisory (`connector-credential-literal`) warns on such a literal. It can only say that `auth.credentialRef` reaches the server over an http transport, because no route exists for stdio.

## Wanted

- Decide a route for stdio credentials that keeps the literal out of metadata, for example `transport.env` entries whose value is resolved from a credential reference at spawn time. The spelling of any new key is a spec-lane question: report options before adding one.
- Then the #29341 advisory's stdio wording can steer to that route.

Dedupe: searched `stdio credentialRef transport env`; nearest #29341, #29342, #28640. **New.**

Links back: #29341, #29424, #28640.
